title: Polynomial-pair bar diagrams and semilinear comparison compatibility
statement:
Let $(A\to B\to C)\to(A'\to B'\to C')$ be a commutative diagram of homomorphisms of commutative rings, with vertical maps $a_0,b_0,c_0$. Choose a common size bound and small identity-cover polynomial presentation sites for both triples. Let $\mathcal E,\mathcal C_i,u_i,F_i,M_i,a,b$ and their primed versions be the pair sites, projection functors and differential short exact sequences of [lem-trf-cotangent-differential-presheaf-ses]. Let $X_i=K_{\mathcal E}^C(M_i)$, $X_i'=K_{\mathcal E'}^{C'}(M_i')$, with $c_i,\alpha_i,c_i',\alpha_i'$ as in [lem-trf-cotangent-bar-term-identifications] and bar notation [def-trf-derived-colimit-bar-system]. Define $v:\mathcal E\to\mathcal E'$ by
$$(P\to B,Q\to C)\longmapsto(P\otimes_A A'\to B',Q\otimes_A A'\to C').$$
Define $v_1(P)=P\otimes_A A'$, $v_2(Q)=Q\otimes_A A'$, $v_3(S)=S\otimes_B B'$, with the induced augmentations. These are functors between the presentation sites. They satisfy $u_1'v=v_1u_1$, $u_2'v=v_2u_2$, and $u_3'v\cong v_3u_3$ via
$$(Q\otimes_A A')\otimes_{P\otimes_A A'}B'\simeq Q\otimes_P B'\simeq(Q\otimes_P B)\otimes_B B'.$$
There are $c_0$-semilinear natural maps $s_i:M_i\to v^{-1}M_i'$ taking the differential generators $\mathrm dp\otimes c$, $\mathrm dq\otimes c$, and $\mathrm d(q\otimes1)\otimes c$ to the corresponding primed differentials tensored with $c_0(c)$. They satisfy $s_2a=(v^{-1}a')s_1$ and $s_3b=(v^{-1}b')s_2$. The maps
$$T_i:(U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)\longmapsto(vU_n\to\cdots\to vU_0,s_{i,U_0}(x))$$
therefore give a morphism of the degreewise short exact sequences $0\to X_1\to X_2\to X_3\to0$ and $0\to X_1'\to X_2'\to X_3'\to0$, with the latter restricted to $C$. If $t_i$ denotes the induced coefficient map on the individual sites (on $F_1\otimes_B C$ for $i=1$), then $c_i'T_i=K(v_i,t_i)c_i$ in $D(C)$, inserting the displayed natural isomorphism for $i=3$. Moreover
$$\alpha_i'T_i=f_i\alpha_i\quad(i=1,2,3)$$
after restriction to $C$, where $f_2:L_{C/A}\to L_{C'/A'}$ and $f_3:L_{C/B}\to L_{C'/B'}$ are the standard cotangent maps and $f_1:L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C\to L_{B'/A'}\otimes_{B'}^{\mathbf L}C'$ is induced by the standard cotangent map for $(a_0,b_0)$ and $c_0$ [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. In bar-tensor coordinates the first comparison has coefficient formula $x\otimes c\mapsto t(x)\otimes c_0(c)$, where $t:F_{B/A}\to v_1^{-1}F_{B'/A'}$ sends $\mathrm dp\otimes r$ to $\mathrm d(p\otimes1)\otimes b_0(r)$. These bar maps and the comparison identities respect identities and composition, with the canonical tensor-associativity identifications. No flatness or injectivity of any vertical map is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08QL (section-functoriality), arbitrary ring squares applied to the pair-site construction of Tag 08QU (lemma-triangle-ses); sites-cohomology Tags 08PG/08PH (example-left-derived-colimits/example-morphism-categories) and 08Q8 (lemma-change-of-rings), explicit semilinear bar compatibility.

proof.text: Work with the common small presentation categories of [lem-trf-cotangent-differential-presheaf-ses]. If $P=A[x_s]$ and $Q=P[y_t]$, extension of coefficients gives $P\otimes_A A'=A'[x_s]$ and $Q\otimes_A A'=(P\otimes_A A')[y_t]$: the inverse maps fix the displayed coefficients and variables. The augmentations send $p\otimes a'$ to $b_0(\epsilon_P(p))a'$ and $q\otimes a'$ to $c_0(\epsilon_Q(q))a'$. The ring squares make them compatible. On arrows use $\phi\otimes1,\psi\otimes1$ and then take opposites; these preserve identity and composition. This constructs $v,v_i$ and the first two projection identities. For the third let $P'=P\otimes_A A'$, $Q'=Q\otimes_A A'$. The balanced algebra map $Q'\otimes_{P'}B'\to Q\otimes_P B'$ sends $(q\otimes a')\otimes b'$ to $q\otimes(a'b')$, and its inverse sends $q\otimes b'$ to $(q\otimes1)\otimes b'$. Next $Q\otimes_P B'\to(Q\otimes_P B)\otimes_B B'$ sends $q\otimes b'$ to $(q\otimes1)\otimes b'$, with inverse $(q\otimes b)\otimes b'\mapsto q\otimes b_0(b)b'$. Their relations, augmentations and arrow compatibility follow on pure tensors. Thus they give the asserted natural isomorphism of third projections. Transport to the chosen skeletons uses these same identifications.

source.place: Tags 08QL (section-functoriality), polynomial coefficient extension; 08QU (lemma-triangle-ses), polynomial-pair values.

proof.text: At a pair $U$ use the three differential descriptions of [lem-trf-cotangent-differential-presheaf-ses]. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] gives the maps $\mathrm d p\mapsto\mathrm d(p\otimes1)$ and $\mathrm d q\mapsto\mathrm d(q\otimes1)$: the latter derivations kill $A$, and the relative one kills $P$ since its target kills $P'$. Extend by $c\mapsto c_0(c)$ to obtain $s_1,s_2,s_3$. Balancing holds because the polynomial-to-coefficient augmentations commute with the ring diagram. In the original third coordinates the formula is $\mathrm d(q\otimes1)\otimes c\mapsto\mathrm d((q\otimes1)\otimes1)\otimes c_0(c)$, followed by the step-1 identification; these generators span, since $\mathrm d(q\otimes b)=b\,\mathrm d(q\otimes1)$ over $B$. For a pair arrow $(\phi,\psi)$, both routes send the first two generators to $\mathrm d(\phi(p)\otimes1)\otimes c_0(c)$ and $\mathrm d(\psi(q)\otimes1)\otimes c_0(c)$, respectively; the third has the same relative formula. This proves naturality. The two routes through $a$ send $\mathrm dp\otimes c$ to $\mathrm d(p\otimes1)\otimes c_0(c)$ in the middle module. The two routes through $b$ send $\mathrm dq\otimes c$ to its relative primed differential tensored with $c_0(c)$. Equality on generators proves both squares.

source.place: Tags 08QU (lemma-triangle-ses), evaluation and differential generator maps; 08QL (section-functoriality).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar] to $v$, the coefficient map $c_0:C\to C'$, and the natural transformations $s_i$. Its semilinear bar formula is exactly $T_i$ in the statement. Its exactness clause takes the two objectwise short exact sequences of [lem-trf-cotangent-differential-presheaf-ses] to degreewise short exact sequences. The squares in step 2 hold in each bar summand, so $T_2K(a)=K(a')T_1$ and $T_3K(b)=K(b')T_2$. In particular this is a morphism of the two short exact sequences after scalar restriction. The chain-map assertion can also be read directly: deleting an internal or leftmost vertex leaves the same coefficient on both sides, and deleting the rightmost vertex commutes with $s_i$ by its naturality; hence every signed face commutes.

source.place: Tags 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits) and 08PH (example-morphism-categories), exactness and chain-map formula.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-cotangent-lower-shriek], $c_i$ reindexes each chain by $u_i$ and retains its coefficient. Define $t_i$ on the individual sites by the differential generator maps just used, and for $i=1$ put $t_1(x\otimes c)=t(x)\otimes c_0(c)$. The formulas are natural by the same universal-property calculation in step 2. For $i=1,2$, $c_i'T_i$ and $K(v_i,t_i)c_i$ reindex the chain by the equal functors $u_i'v=v_iu_i$ and apply the same coefficient map, so agree already on complexes. For $i=3$ use the step-1 natural isomorphism. It takes the image of $q\otimes b$ to $(q\otimes1)\otimes b_0(b)$, and thus identifies the coefficient maps on $\mathrm d(q\otimes1)\otimes c$. The natural-isomorphism clause of [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar] makes the two resulting bar maps equal in $D(C)$. This proves all three $c_i'T_i=K(v_i,t_i)c_i$ identities with the stated third identification.

source.place: Tag 08PH (example-morphism-categories), reindexing; cotangent Tag 08QW (lemma-triangle-compute-lower-shriek), comparisons; natural-isomorphism bar homotopy as in cited node.

proof.text: For $i=2$ apply the arbitrary-square identity of [lem-trf-cotangent-sheaf-model] to $(A\to C)\to(A'\to C')$; for $i=3$ apply it to $(B\to C)\to(B'\to C')$. The site functors and coefficient maps in that identity are precisely $v_i,t_i$. It gives $\theta_i'K(v_i,t_i)=f_i\theta_i$, with all target scalars restricted along $c_0$. By [lem-trf-cotangent-bar-term-identifications], $\alpha_i=\theta_i c_i$ and $\alpha_i'=\theta_i'c_i'$ for these two indices. Substituting step 4 yields $\alpha_i'T_i=\theta_i'K(v_i,t_i)c_i=f_i\alpha_i$. The cited square identity identifies these $f_i$ with the standard-resolution maps, not merely some maps with the same cohomology.

source.place: Tag 08QL (section-functoriality), two descriptions of the canonical map; Tag 08QX (proposition-triangle), second and third identifications.

proof.text: Write $H=L\pi_{1,!}^B F_1$ and $H'=L\pi_{1,!}^{B'}F_1'$, and let $h:H\to H'$ be the semilinear bar map for $v_1,t$. Put $J=K_{\mathcal C_1}^C(F_1\otimes_B C)$, and let $\beta:J\simeq H\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C$ be the bar-tensor comparison (similarly for primes). The flat-value hypothesis needed in [lem-trf-derived-colimit-change-rings] follows directly from [lem-trf-cotangent-bar-term-identifications] for $F_1$ and $F_1'$. Apply its compatibility with indexing functors and coefficient-ring squares to $(B\to C)\to(B'\to C')$. It gives $\beta'K(v_1,t_1)=\widetilde h\beta$, where $\widetilde h$ is the induced derived tensor map. On a bar generator both routes are $(v_1P_\bullet,t(x))\otimes c_0(c)$, proving the requested coefficient formula as well. The square identity of [lem-trf-cotangent-sheaf-model] for $(A\to B)\to(A'\to B')$ is $\theta_{B'/A'}h=f_{a_0,b_0}^{\mathrm{std}}\theta_{B/A}$. Its image under the induced derived tensor maps gives $(\theta_{B'/A'}\otimes^{\mathbf L}1)\widetilde h=f_1(\theta_{B/A}\otimes^{\mathbf L}1)$. Finally [lem-trf-cotangent-bar-term-identifications] defines $\alpha_1=(\theta_{B/A}\otimes^{\mathbf L}1)\beta c_1$. Substitute step 4 and the last two identities into this composite to obtain $\alpha_1'T_1=f_1\alpha_1$. No replacement of derived tensor by ordinary tensor for an arbitrary complex has been used.

source.place: Tag 08Q8 (lemma-change-of-rings), flat-presheaf bar comparison; cotangent Tags 08QL and 08QX (section-functoriality, proposition-triangle), first comparison.

proof.text: For an identity diagram each differential generator is fixed, and $(p\otimes a)\mapsto pa$ identifies its polynomial extension functor with the identity. For two composable diagrams the tensor-associativity map $(P\otimes_A A')\otimes_{A'}A''\to P\otimes_A A''$ sends $(p\otimes a')\otimes a''$ to $p\otimes a'a''$; on differential coefficients the composite sends $\mathrm dp\otimes c$ to $\mathrm d(p\otimes1)\otimes(c_0'c_0)(c)$. The same check applies to $Q$ and $Q\otimes_P B$ and to the step-1 third-projection isomorphism, on their pure tensors. Thus the $s_i$ compose under these natural identifications. Identity and composition of the $T_i$ now follow from [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar], with its natural-isomorphism clause where skeletons require it. The standard cotangent maps obey identity and composition by [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]; the change-of-rings identifications obey the coefficient-square compatibility of [lem-trf-derived-colimit-change-rings]. Consequently the comparison identities in steps 4--6 compose by substitution and associativity. None of these arguments assumes flatness or injectivity of the vertical maps: the only flatness invoked was that of the polynomial differential values.
